newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia 10-yr bond sustains break of 7.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australia 10-yr bond sustains break of 7.0 pct.

text.p: *Australian 10-year bond yields sustained a break below 7.0 percent for the first time since February 1994 as concerns of a Fed tightening lessen, leaving scope for the RBA to ease.
*10-year spread to US touches lowest level in over a decade.
Australian 10-year bond yields sustained a break below the 7.0 percent barrier to close at their lowest level since February 1994.

A rally in U.S. Treasuries on Friday following a weak U.S. Producer Price Index gave an already bullish local market a further boost as it was seen lessening the chance of a tightening by the U.S. Fed at its July policy-making meeting.
If this proves the case it is seen increasing the chances of an easing by Australia's Reserve Bank, if it has not already loosened policy by then.
"I think 7.0 percent is fair value...unless there is more than one more rate cut out there," said David Bassanese, senior economist at Bankers Trust Australia.
Long yields have dropped more than one full point in just over two months as, apart from the housing sector, the data flow has been fairly weak, not least last week's labour force data.

This data saw the debt market rally strongly last week with September bill futures all but price in a 50 basis point easing. However, the market now finds itself in a slight quandry in the absence of any key local data this week and if the RBA does not make a pre-July 1 board meeting easing.

"There is little domestic data this week with key U.S. numbers likely to have a bigger influence on the market. Nevertheless, the 9.30 a.m. screen watching ritual is likely to continue," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank, refering to the RBA's usual policy announcement time.
Indeed, the U.S. faces CPI, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilization for May on Tuesday alone.
However, uncertainty in Europe over the single currency issue is likely to remain supportive for Australia debt along with other dollar bloc currencies, analysts said.
The local market put in a strong performance against the U.S. in early trading which saw the 10-year spread dip below 50 basis points, its lowest level in over a decade, analysts said.
They added that this tightening trend could continue on Australia's better inflation outlook against the U.S. and due to the RBA's perceived policy easing bias against the Fed's tightening bias.

"A (spread) move to 25 basis points could well happen if there is evidence of employment remaining weak, and inflation and wages are still low," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.
The local short end gave up some ground to Canada, which outperformed on waning fears of a U.S. tightening following last Friday's U.S. PPI.

June bond contracts expired at midday, but not before the 10-year position made a 3-1/4 year higher of 93.090. The September contract is trading at a small discount to June and still needs to overcome the market's previous 93.015 peak seen in December last year. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
